Preliminary Study for Posture Monitoring in Driving Condition Using 
Piezoresistive Film-based Force Sensor 
 
Sangjin Han1, Jewon Son1, Miri Kim1 and Hangsik Shin1 1Department of Biomedical Engineering, Chonnam National University, Yeosu, Republic of Korea 
E-mail: hangsik.shin@jnu.ac.kr 
Abstract— We develop the pressure variation 
monitoring system using a piezoresistive film-based 
sensor array for practical use in a car . We 
implemented the sensor array in the car seat, and 
investigated the change of pressure distribution 
according to posture changes . As a result, we 
statistically validated that the proposed system 
could measure the pressure variatio n with high 
significance. 
Keywords— Driving Safety, Force Sensor, 
Piezoresistive Sensor, Posture Monitoring 
I. INTRODUCTION 
National Highway Traffic Safety Administration 
reports that the drowsy driving causes 100,000 of traffic 
accidents and 72,500 of road causalities per year [1,2]. 
This shows that the driver’s fatigue is a critical factor of 
car accidents. In previous research, it has been proven 
that the driver’s posture is closely related to the fatigue 
[3], thus we can estimate the driver’s fatigue by 
measuring posture. In this research, as a preliminary 
study for driver’s fatigue measurement, we developed 
the car seat embedded pressure measurement system 
and validate its significance in posture monitoring. 
II. FORCE SENSING PLATFORM 
A. Piezoresistive Force Sensor 
To measure the force from the driver, we designed the 
textile force measurement sensor. Developed sensor has 
layered architecture to measure the resistance variation 
by changing force on the surface contacted to the body. 
The architecture of the sensor is represented in Fig. 1. 
We use VelostatTM film (3M Co., Minneapolis, Minn.) 
to measure the force variation, and surround it with 
copper foil to connect to the electric wire. 
Polyvinylchloride film was used as an insulator and 
cover of conductive part. Each sensor is fabricated as a 
square shape with 12 cm length of each side. 
 
Fig. 1. Architecture of the developed piezoresistive film-
based force sensor 
B. Pressure Distribution Measurement Platform 
To measure the force distribution of contact surface in 
sitting condition, we place 8 sensors in the car seat. 
Sensors are arranged in square, and each row and 
column is consisted with 3 sections. But, the sensor is 
not placed on the FC (Front-Central) because motions 
may less affect FC. Fig. 2 shows the sensor placement 
in the car seat. 
 
Fig.2. Force sensor placement in car seat (F: Front, B: Back, 
L: Left, R: Right, C: Center) 
III. RESULTS 
In sitting condition, five subjects change their position 
to tilting left/right and leaning forward. Tilt angle was 
controlled between 15º and 30º, and the test was 
repeated by 10 times per subject. Force variation was 
recorded simultaneously. We calculated the difference 
between the recorded value of tilting and normal 
condition to definitize the variation from the posture 
changes. The average values of left (ml), right (mr), 
front (mf) and back (mb)-side sensors were calculated to 
compare the pressure difference by direction. For 
example, ml - mr and mb - mf were calculated to detect 
left/right tilting and forward leaning, respectively. To 
validate the pressure variation according to the posture 
change, the differences were compared with the 
differences of normal condition. As a result, significant 
force changes were found. Pearson’s R was 0.996, 0993 
and 0.996 in left, right tilting and forward leaning, 
respectively. (p is less than 0.001 in every case) 
IV. CONCLUSION 
In this research, we developed piezoresistive film -
based pressure variation sensing platform and 
confirmed the feasibility. We expect that proposed 
sensing platform would be utilized to measure the 
driver’s posture and fatigue in our future work.
